report.summary: Reviewed chunk 1 of daedalus/mapping/drift.py; enumerated constants, module docstring claims, and schema comments.

handoff.purpose: Module header: docstring, imports, constants, and documentation/reachability classification constants.

symbols.note: Relative path to the committed snapshot.

claims.text: A hand-written feature inventory listed 136 features, 8 islands and 2 dark switches. Six hours later a deep read of the same tree found 827, 55 and 51.
claims.why: Historical numbers; no data in this chunk.

claims.text: this module compares the CURRENT generated state against a COMMITTED snapshot (``docs/architecture-state.json``) and fails when they disagree.
claims.why: Comparison logic is in later chunks; only SNAPSHOT_REL is defined here.

claims.text: The snapshot is deliberately small, sorted and free of timestamps
claims.why: Snapshot writing/formatting is in later chunks.

claims.text: This module DERIVES NOTHING ITSELF. Islands come from reach.analyse; switches come from switches.analyse; both are the same reports the page renders, computed once and passed in.
claims.why: No function bodies in this chunk; imports of reach_mod and switches_mod exist but no derivation logic is visible.

claims.text: this file used to run its own reachability scan and its own environment scan, and the two implementations disagreed on the same tree -- the gate saw 11 islands where the page saw 6, sharing not one member, and the gate's dark half reported 0 where the switch engine reported 15.
claims.why: Historical anecdote; no code in this chunk.

claims.text: UNREACHED = every reach class that means "no entry point gets here", UNREACHED_CLASSES, split across THREE lists ... islands reach's island + orphan ... unknown reach could not tell ... shims a re-export nothing reaches.
claims.why: ISLAND_CLASSES = ('island','orphan'), UNKNOWN_CLASSES = ('unknown',), SHIM_CLASSES = ('shim',), and UNREACHED_CLASSES concatenates them; matches the docstring's mapping.

claims.text: These three used to be one list containing only the first, and the other two were dropped on the floor ... Every unreached module is now counted, in exactly one of the three lists, and counts['unreached'] is their total -- the number the page has to add up to.
claims.why: The claim about counts['unreached'] and the three lists being exhaustive is not verifiable from constants alone; needs function bodies.

claims.text: DARK = switches' dark verdict, MINUS the ones it classifies secret, MINUS the ones documented BY THIS FILE'S RULE (see DOCUMENTED, below).
claims.why: No dark-switch computation in this chunk.

claims.text: Darkness itself -- off by default, no fallback, in a boolean position -- is decided in exactly one place, daedalus.mapping.switches; both subtractions are over fields that engine already computed
claims.why: The switch engine is in another module; this chunk only imports switches_mod.

claims.text: The secret carve-out is a judgement call worth arguing with: an absent API key is not a dark feature, it is a documented feature that is merely unconfigured, and daedalus doctor is where that belongs.
claims.why: No doctor logic in this chunk.

claims.text: Reachability is the transitive closure of the import graph from DISCOVERED entry points (console scripts, __main__.py, __main__ guards, CLI dispatch branches, HTTP routes, poll loops).
claims.why: Reachability logic is in reach module, not this chunk.

claims.text: A module reached only by its own test is STILL AN ISLAND here, and it is reported as one -- but under its own kind, TEST_ONLY, which does not block.
claims.why: No TEST_ONLY constant or handling in this chunk; REACHED_CLASSES includes 'test' but no TEST_ONLY constant is defined here.

claims.text: An environment variable that (a) is consumed as a BOOLEAN GATE, (b) defaults OFF with no fallback, and (c) is not documented. (a) and (b) are switches's judgement, verbatim.
claims.why: Definition of dark switch is in switches module; this chunk does not implement it.

claims.text: (c) is this file's, and it is stricter than "the token appears somewhere" ... A switch counts as documented when, in a doc that is not generated and outside every fenced code block, it appears in a form an operator would actually type or an author would emphasise -- NAME=..., export NAME, set NAME, $env:NAME, "environment variable NAME", `NAME` or **NAME** -- and beside at least MIN_DOC_DESC_CHARS characters of other prose, on that line or the next non-empty one.
claims.why: The documentation-detection logic is not in this chunk; only constants MIN_DOC_DESC_CHARS, GENERATED_DOCS, _GENERATED_MARK, _FENCE_RE are defined.

claims.text: Code fences are excluded because a fenced sample is where a name most often appears without being explained, and GENERATED_DOCS is excluded because daedalus map renders that file INTO the artifact this gate guards -- counting it would let the page document its own findings away.
claims.why: The exclusion logic is not in this chunk; _FENCE_RE and GENERATED_DOCS exist but no scanning code.

claims.text: This is deliberately not "one designated inventory file with a description", which would be stronger still. It is not, because introducing that file is a documentation change outside this module, and a gate that fails until an unrelated file is created gets turned off rather than satisfied.
claims.why: Design rationale; no code to verify.

claims.text: TIER 1 -- TEMPORARY, DATED, SELF-RESURFACING (acceptances in the snapshot): ... EXPLICIT AND GREPPABLE ... RECORDS WHY AND WHEN -- why under MIN_WHY_CHARS characters is rejected, and both dates are required. ... BOUND TO THE CALENDAR ... until is capped at MAX_HORIZON_DAYS past since AND since may not be in the future. ... Past until the acceptance stops suppressing and the underlying item comes back with the acceptance's own prose attached ... An accepted item is NEVER written into the baseline (see write_snapshot). ... An acceptance that matches nothing is a STALE ACCEPTANCE and blocks.
claims.why: Acceptance validation logic is in later chunks; MIN_WHY_CHARS and MAX_HORIZON_DAYS are defined here but no validation code.

claims.text: TIER 2 -- PERMANENT, BY REVIEWED DIFF (--refresh). Deleting the acceptance and re-baselining moves the item into islands/dark_switches and bumps counts. There is no expiry, and there does not need to be: the change is a line in a committed file, in a diff, with the count moving next to it.
claims.why: refresh logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Every mechanical list is covered by a DIGEST_KEY over the canonical bytes, so hand-editing islands or dark_switches to pre-seed a finding into the baseline is an INVALID SNAPSHOT rather than a silent pass.
claims.why: Digest logic is not in this chunk; hashlib is imported but no digest function is defined here.

claims.text: The lists are additionally required to be internally coherent (islands, unknown and shims are subsets of modules; test_only is a subset of their union) and grounded in reality (dark_switches must name variables the code still reads).
claims.why: Validation logic is in later chunks.

claims.text: WHAT THAT SENTENCE IS ALLOWED TO CLAIM is exactly this: every verb in this subsystem that READS a snapshot re-derives the digest first and refuses a mismatch. check reports INVALID SNAPSHOT. render.accept -- which inherits the mechanical lists verbatim in order not to bank unrelated drift -- refuses to inherit them at all unless the digest it is inheriting verifies ... refresh does not need the check: it rescans and overwrites every mechanical list from the tree.
claims.why: check, render.accept, and refresh are not in this chunk.

claims.text: It does not stop somebody who runs Python to re-compute the digest, and it is not meant to: the control on a deliberate re-baseline is the reviewed diff, which is Tier 2 and works exactly as designed.
claims.why: Design rationale; no code.

claims.text: DAEDALUS_IGNORE and .daedalusignore narrow the structural index. Since the gate now reads the tree through reach, which walks the filesystem itself, they cannot narrow what the gate sees -- but the configuration is recorded in the snapshot and compared on every run anyway, so that a green result taken under a narrowed configuration can never be indistinguishable from a green result taken under a clean one.
claims.why: Ignore handling is not in this chunk; IGNORE_FILENAME and IGNORE_ENV are defined but no logic.

claims.text: A missing snapshot is NOT a pass. Both entry points refuse it: daedalus map --check exits non-zero, and python -m daedalus.mapping.drift does too. Writing a baseline is an explicit named action (--init, --refresh, or a plain daedalus map), because rm docs/architecture-state.json must not be a way to get a green run.
claims.why: Entry points are in later chunks.

claims.text: This is a CI GATE, NOT A PRE-COMMIT HOOK. A full run parses every Python file in the tree twice (reachability and switches) and takes seconds, not milliseconds.
claims.why: Performance characteristics are not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: schema-1 baseline cannot be compared against a schema-2 run -- the lists mean different things.
claims.why: Schema comparison logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: A schema-2 baseline has no place to put any of that, so it is refused rather than read as "those lists are empty".
claims.why: Schema refusal logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Within 3, additively: repo_state records WHICH TREE was scanned and is covered by the digest. Not a version bump, because the lists still mean what they meant -- a schema-3 baseline without it simply cannot answer the freshness question, which snapshot_freshness reports as "not fresh" rather than pretending otherwise.
claims.why: snapshot_freshness is not in this chunk.

claims.text: The teeth. An acceptance may not be written further out than this, so no acceptance can outlive a release cycle without a human retyping the reason.
claims.why: The constant exists, but the enforcement logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: "wip" is not a reason. Short enough to be typeable, long enough to be a sentence.
claims.why: The constant exists, but the validation logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: orphan is reach's strictly-worse island (imports nothing, imported by nothing, untested); the remedy is the same, so the gate does not split them.
claims.why: The classification of orphan comes from reach; not verifiable here.

claims.text: What may never happen again is a reach class that means unreached and appears in none of them.
claims.why: This is a design constraint; enforcement is in tests not in this chunk.

claims.text: Together with UNREACHED_CLASSES this must cover reach.CLASSES exactly; the property is asserted in the tests, because a new reach class silently landing outside both sets is precisely how two classes got dropped the first time.
claims.why: The assertion is in tests, not in this chunk.

claims.text: Counting a mention here would let the page document away its own findings.
claims.why: The actual exclusion logic is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Prose that has to sit beside the name before a mention counts as an explanation. Roughly "five words": long enough that a bare token and a two-word label both fail, short enough that a real one-line entry passes.
claims.why: The constant is defined, but the description-detection logic is not in this chunk.

observations.what: Docstring makes multiple claims about behavior that cannot be verified in this chunk; only constants and imports are present.
REACHED_CLASSES includes 'test' but the docstring mentions TEST_ONLY as a distinct kind; no TEST_ONLY constant is defined in this chunk.
Constants ISLAND_CLASSES, UNKNOWN_CLASSES, SHIM_CLASSES are defined as tuples; UNREACHED_CLASSES is their concatenation, which matches the docstring's three-list split.
